title: Pain free wrist curls: the finger curls solution for bigger forearms
summary: NH demonstrates finger curls as a pain-free replacement for wrist curls, which gave him wrist pain. He pairs heavy partial-range behind-the-back standing wrist curls with full-range finger curls, pronated (two hands, straight bar) and supinated (one hand, EZ bar), where the wrist curls in as the fingers close. Programming is 4-6 sets of 6-12 reps, supersetted, on upper days.
claims: Deadlifts and pulls alone don't grow the forearms; you need wrist flexion work
Painful wrist curls can turn into tendinitis and hurt pressing strength, costing upper-body size
The only wrist curl that ever worked for him was seated with a fixed dumbbell and his arm braced on his leg
The wrist's full range of motion isn't needed to train the forearm; the extended bottom position, with the load pulling diagonally on the hand, causes the pain
Standing wrist curls behind the back avoid the thighs, allow heavy partial-range overload, and work well with a thumbless grip
Do pronated finger curls with two hands on a straight bar so the bar doesn't rotate
Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then close the fingers so the wrist curls in at the end; this gives full range without wrist pain
His favourite forearm isolation is the one-handed supinated finger curl with an EZ bar, keeping the wrist from bending back
Program finger curls at 4-6 sets of 6-10 or 8-12 reps, supersetted since they aren't taxing
Start forearm isolation at 3 sets a week and build up
He does wrist flexion on upper days and isometric grip holds on lower days
Don't keep suffering through a lift that hurts; pain means it doesn't work for you
exercises: fixed dumbbell, forearm braced on leg
only wrist curl that didn't hurt him; standard versions cause wrist pain
straight bar, partial range, thumbless grip, load heavy
overloads forearm without thigh obstruction or wrist pain
two hands, straight bar, roll bar to fingertips then curl fingers and wrist
one hand, EZ bar, open fingers without cocking the wrist back, close into a curl
his favourite forearm isolation; huge pump, pain-free
